text:
margot: FYI customer reported a burst of 502s and truncated streaming responses from hosted API during a large prompt run. they see body cut off mid-token and client gets 502. ticket #12489

margot: customer says calls are fine at low QPS, spikes at ~80qps cause ~5% of requests to 502, others succeed. happened after model swap to rwd-v2-13b.

margot: pasted curl they used (sanitized auth):

margot: ```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer XXXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-v2-13b","input":"<very long prompt>"}' \
  --http2
```

margot: customer also included a short tcpdump showing FIN from our edge right before body truncated.

devon: thanks. can you paste a request id or trace id? any upstream trace?

margot: two sample req ids: req_01FZ9... and req_01FZB... attached envoy log lines from eu1-edge: 

margot: ```
[2026-03-18T21:12:09.123Z] external_service: upstream reset before response complete, downstream 200, upstream 499
[2026-03-18T21:12:09.124Z] envoy: upstream premature close while reading response body
```

ingress-bot: automatically correlated trace: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/01FZ9. latency topology shows spikes hitting the ingress h2 pool.

devon: pattern looks like upstream closed connection while streaming. could be backpressure or conn window exhaustion on the upstream pool. Did customer set Transfer-Encoding chunked?

margot: customer says they use SDK which streams and uses http2, not explicit chunked header.

samir: i've seen similar when nginx/edge drops long-lived streams if keepalive config is low and pool has many concurrent streams. also model change -> slightly longer time-to-first-byte and our window/backpressure thresholds may trigger ejection.

elena: can we reproduce? i can run a load test that streams a long prompt concurrently. quick test plan: 1) reproduce with http2 streaming client 2) ramp to 80-100 qps 3) capture envoy logs and upstream behavior 4) try toggling proxy_read_timeout and h2 window settings

oncall: assign to devon + samir. mitigation for customer: enable automatic retry/fallback to smaller model for that tenant or reduce client concurrency. i'll message CS to suggest temporary retry logic server-side until we confirm root cause.

devon: trying quick repro locally now. sharing script (node-based simplified):

devon: ```js
// simplified repro, uses http2 sessions and sends large JSON then prematurely closes stream
const http2 = require('http2');
const client = http2.connect('https://api.redwood.ai');
const req = client.request({':method':'POST', ':path':'/v1/outputs', 'authorization': 'Bearer xxxx', 'content-type':'application/json'});
req.write(JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-v2-13b', input: 'A'.repeat(200000)}));
// simulate client abort in middle of send for spike
setTimeout(()=>{ req.close(); client.close(); }, 80);
```

devon: early results: at ~90qps sim i see envoys returning 502 with upstream reset when I abort mid-send. if client closes early we produce env reset but customer said body truncated while they didn't abort.

samir: that points to upstream/keystore or midproxy doing aggressive drain. any recent keystore or TLS rotation in the timeframe?

margot: ops: we rotated TLS keystore on eu1 on 2026-03-18 20:50UTC (small keystore refresh). customer issues started ~21:10 UTC.

devon: that aligns. keystore rotation can cause brief conn churn if in-flight streams hit a server that restarted sessions; some h2 sessions might be reset and cause truncated bodies. envoy log 'upstream reset before response complete' fits.

elena: mitigation: we can rollout a soft patch to edge to drain gracefully: mark new nodes as warm and allow existing h2 sessions to finish. also increase proxy_read_timeout to 120s from 30s for streaming endpoints temporarily.

oncall: i'll push a short-lived config change to eu1 edge: increase proxy_read_timeout and bump h2 connection drain grace. schedule window NOW.

ingress-bot: deploy started: edge-config/eu1/2026-03-18/ingress-timeout-bump to canary (5% nodes).

devon: after canary, 1 hour of ramp tests show error rate drop from 4.8% -> 0.3% for streaming requests under the same load.

margot: CS notified customer of temporary mitigation and asked them to test. awaiting confirmation.

samir: root cause hypothesis: TLS keystore rotation triggered server-side process replacement in subset of edge fleet. in-flight HTTP/2 streams were terminated by replaced upstreams causing 502 and truncated bodies. coupled with aggressive read timeouts caused the client-observed truncation.

elena: action items:
- (devon) add additional logging to correlate keystore-rotate events to upstream resets (PR #4321)
- (samir) propose change to rollout choreography to keep old instances draining h2 for X minutes (ticket RW-789)
- (oncall) revert timeout bump after stable window and add playbook note
- (margot) follow up with customer and close ticket after confirmation

devon: quick snippet of envoy metric we looked at: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_503: 120 -> suspicious cluster state changes.

margot: customer retested and reports success with <1% errors after we applied config. they will confirm tomorrow during peak. CS will keep watch.

oncall: closing loop here, no further action until prod validation looks good for 24h. marking as monitoring.

margot: thanks all :thumbsup:
